edgeFunctions.name: enrich-cast-cron
edgeFunctions.purpose: Server-side sweep that backfills "Cast & Creative" for theatre tickets. WHY THIS EXISTS: cast enrichment used to be client-on-demand ONLY — the event-details screen called enrich-cast when a theatre ticket had no cast. So any theatre ticket never opened in-app on a cast-enabled build stayed empty forever (in prod, 20 of 25 theatre tickets had zero cast). This runs server-side on a schedule and enriches every theatre ticket regardless of how it was created (gmail / imap / photo / manual / calendar). It does the SAME enrichment as enrich-cast INLINE (Wikidata grounding + Claude + the is_known guard, via the shared ./core.ts) rather than calling enrich-cast over HTTP: that hop 401'd at the gateway because enrich-cast is verify_jwt=true and a service-role Bearer isn't accepted there. Doing it inline with the service client also needs no per-ticket ownership check (this is a trusted backfill)

edgeFunctions.name: enrich-lineup

The client ignores the flag (it only reads `lineup`); the enrichment worker uses it to back off and retry instead of marking the job done. Without this the two cases are indistinguishable — an Anthropic 429 would permanently converge a real festival to "no lineup", which is exactly the empty-vs-throttled trap documented in the worker's runGeocode.

edgeFunctions.name: enrich-sweep

edgeFunctions.name: enrichment-worker
edgeFunctions.purpose: The single enrichment worker — drains the enrichment_jobs queue for every kind. See 20260813230000_enrichment_pipeline.sql for the why. Each tick: discover work (enqueue_enrichment_jobs), then per kind claim a small PACED batch and run its handler, marking each job done (attempted — data found or definitively none) or a transient retry. Because a 429 / 5xx becomes a backed-off retry rather than a "done", a burst can never silently mark a resolvable item unresolved, and the per-kind batch caps keep us under every provider's rate limit. Adding an enrichment kind = one handler here + one INSERT in enqueue_enrichment_jobs(). Phase 1 covers geocode (reuses geocode-venues/core.ts) and sports_result (drives sports-score-lookup). Auth: verify_jwt=false (config.toml) + shared x-cron-secret.

Gated three ways so it can only reach the right people: (1) the uploader must be SHARING event photos — otherwise co-attendees literally can't see them, so a "come look" push would be a dead end; (2) friendship; (3) shared attendance (the recipient has their own ticket for the same canonical event). Deduped to one alert per (adder, recipient, event) via sent_event_photo_alerts, so re-uploading to the same album doesn't re-ping. verify_jwt stays TRUE (default): the caller's JWT is required for the gates. edgeFunctions.purpose: Push + inbox notification for a new direct message. Called by the SENDER's client right after inserting a message. We authenticate the caller, confirm they and the recipient are accepted friends (mirroring the direct_messages insert RLS, so this can't be used to spam strangers), then hand off to send-notification which writes the inbox row, respects the user's notification_preferences, and sends the Expo push when a token exists.

edgeFunctions.name: notify-status
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push + inbox when a friend posts an event status (retention Phase 3, social loop). Called by the POSTER's client right after inserting the status. Gated on BOTH friendship AND shared attendance (the recipient must have their own ticket for the same canonical event) — so this can only reach people who were actually there, never broadcast a status to strangers. verify_jwt stays TRUE (default): the caller's JWT is required for the friendship check, exactly like notify-message. Do NOT add this function to config.toml's verify_jwt=false list.

edgeFunctions.name: notify-tag-prompt
edgeFunctions.purpose: Push a "tag your friend" nudge when a new ticket overlaps a friend's event. Client-invoked by the NEW ticket's owner right after creating it (mirrors notify-message). We authenticate the caller, confirm they own the (active, titled) ticket, and — only if the owner's OWN privacy allows being surfaced (mirroring suggest_event_attendees: allow_tagging + share_events + not only_me) — notify each accepted friend who already has the SAME event and isn't already linked to it. "Same event" is the canonical eventDedupeKey (shared catalog event_id, else title + DAY), NOT a raw lowercased title — the exact match public.suggest_event_attendees uses. A raw title match both over-fired (a friend's SAME show on a DIFFERENT date got a bogus "you're both going" push — the "Dave went to Hamilton on a different date" report) and under-fired (a "TICKET:"-prefixed or reformatted title missed a real overlap).

sharedModules.purpose: The external-API cost/health ledger (`api_usage_log`). Two entry points: logApiUsage(admin, entry) — the original, for callers that already hold a service-role client. trackedFetch(url, init, meta) — wraps one outbound provider call and records it. Use this for new instrumentation: it needs no client, so a function does not have to build a service-role client just to log, and a call site stays one line. This file deliberately imports NOTHING. `_shared` modules that jest loads must not pull in `https://esm.sh/...` (jest cannot resolve it), which is why logApiUsage takes an untyped `admin` and why trackedFetch talks to PostgREST over raw fetch — the same trick notify.ts uses.

sharedModules.name: confidence.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Multi-signal confidence (beta #6). A single event can be evidenced by several INDEPENDENT sources — a Gmail/IMAP receipt, a device-calendar entry, a matched photo, an existing setlist. When more than one corroborates the SAME event, our confidence that it's real should climb toward certainty. We treat each source as independent evidence and combine with noisy-OR: combined = 1 - Π(1 - confidence_i) Two independent 0.7 signals → 0.91; three mid signals → ~0.94; a lone 0.55 stays 0.55. This is what pushes corroborated events toward the 90-100% the beta wants, while a single weak signal stays low. Repeated hits from the SAME source collapse to their strongest single confidence first (two Gmail emails for one show are one piece of evidence, not two).

sharedModules.name: contentAlert.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Build the push/inbox copy for a post-event content alert. Pure — no side effects, no I/O — so the exact wording is unit-tested. `eventTitle` is the ticket title (e.g. "Phish at MSG"); a blank/unknown title falls back to a neutral phrase rather than an empty string.

sharedModules.name: crypto.ts
sharedModules.purpose: AES-256-GCM application-layer encryption for credentials stored at rest (Gmail OAuth tokens, IMAP passwords). The key lives only in the edge-function runtime (TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY secret), never in the database — so a DB dump or a leaked row reveals only ciphertext. Satisfies CASA Tier 2 / OWASP ASVS V6 (cryptographic storage of sensitive data). ── Key rotation ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────── Rotating the key used to be silently destructive. Every stored value was "enc:v1:<data>" with no record of WHICH key produced it, and only one key was ever loaded — so the moment TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY changed, every existing credential became permanently undecryptable, and the only symptom was `OperationError: Decryption failed` deep in a scan function. That is exactly what happened on 2026-08-08: six mailbox credentials died at once and it took reading edge-function lo

sharedModules.purpose: Remove a junk "TICKET:"-style lead, preserving the rest verbatim (case + spacing).

sharedModules.name: imapAllowlist.ts
sharedModules.purpose: Throws if the host/port is not an approved IMAP endpoint. Call before persisting or connecting to a user-supplied IMAP host.

sharedModules.name: imapError.ts
sharedModules.purpose: A rich, credential-safe one-line diagnostic for an IMAP / ImapFlow error. scan-imap used to record only `err.message`, which for ImapFlow is the generic "Command failed" on almost every failure. That cannot tell a REVOKED / wrong app password (`authenticationFailed`, code AUTHENTICATIONFAILED) from a TLS / network fault (ETIMEDOUT, ECONNREFUSED, …) — so a Yahoo connection that failed every scheduled scan for two weeks left `scan_runs.error_message = "IMAP connection failed: Command failed"` and nobody could see why. ImapFlow carries the real cause in PROPERTIES, and its error `response`/`responseText` are the SERVER's reply lines (e.g. "NO [AUTHENTICATIONFAILED]"), never the password the client sent — so they are safe to persist. Same lesson as store-email-connection/core.ts's errorText(): read the properties, not just `.message`.

Reuses the same Vault secret ('scan_cron_secret') and edge CRON_SECRET as the scheduled-scans job, so no new secret is introduced. Runs daily at 17:00 UTC.

Event-anchored statuses ("stories") — see modules/status/*. A status always references a real ticket/event; the event fields are denormalized at insert time (mirrors the denormalized `tickets` table) so a viewer never needs a join and the card survives the ticket being deleted.

Populated lazily (write-through on first tap) and proactively at ticket creation (lib/enrichTicketImage.ts). Distinct from `external_id`, which the Ticketmaster-sourced discover flow already uses.

Security hardening: stop PII over-exposure on public.users and lock down anon-callable SECURITY DEFINER data functions. And `find_users_by_phones` / `get_public_ticket_stats` (both SECURITY DEFINER, so they bypass RLS) were callable by the `anon` role, whose key ships inside the app and is trivially extractable -> phone->identity scraping and attendance enumeration with no account required.

Performance + hardening pass (Supabase advisors). 1) auth_rls_initplan: RLS policies that call auth.uid()/is_active_admin() per-row are wrapped in a scalar subselect so the planner evaluates them once per query instead of once per row. Semantics are identical. 2) Revoke the REST RPC EXECUTE grant on trigger-only functions that were never meant to be callable directly (finished in the companion migration 20260712121000, which revokes from PUBLIC -- the grant these functions actually hold; revoking from anon/authenticated alone is a no-op).

Their EXECUTE grant is held via PUBLIC (not anon/authenticated directly), so the companion migration's revoke-from-anon/authenticated was a no-op. Revoke from PUBLIC so they can no longer be invoked over /rest/v1/rpc/*. Triggers run as the function owner and do not require EXECUTE, so trigger behavior is unaffected.

Explicit-share friend privacy: connecting with someone no longer auto-shares ALL of your events. Previously `friends_can_view_tickets` let any accepted friend SELECT every one of a user's tickets. Now a friend can view a ticket only if they were explicitly tagged/shared on it (a ticket_attendees row with user_id = them). Own tickets stay visible via tickets_select_own.

Resumable email sweeps. The original Gmail importer capped the first listMessages() pass at the 500 newest query matches, then saved gmail_history_id and switched every later scan to incremental history. For users with deep matching back-catalogues, older ticket emails were never fetched and then became permanently unreachable because incremental sync only sees new mail. Existing connections default initial_sweep_complete=false on purpose: their back-catalogue was not proven read under an uncapped algorithm, even if they already have a history cursor. We deliberately do NOT wipe gmail_history_id; it remains the right incremental cursor once the resumable sweep reaches the end.

Scan run audit trail. This table records one compact row per email scan invocation. Edge functions use the service role for writes; users only get owner-scoped read access so support can expose/inspect scan history without widening access to another user's mail metadata.

Guideline 1.2 moderation: user blocks + content reports. Additive + guarded: is_blocked_with() returns false while user_blocks is empty, so the policy guards below are no-ops for all existing users until a block exists.

Which team you were rooting for is a personal opinion, but it was stored on sports_stats, which is UNIQUE (ticket_id) -- one row per ticket, holding objective game data (scores, lineups) fetched from the sports API. Short codes for shared event links. A shared link used to carry the whole event in its query string, because the recipient does not own the ticket and RLS gives them nothing to load. Access is via SECURITY DEFINER functions only; the table itself is unreachable from the client. A plain RLS "select where code = ..." policy would NOT work: RLS filters rows, it does not require you to know a code, so any authenticated user could select the whole table. Knowing the code has to be the thing that returns the row, which means a function.

Make a failed scan visible. scan_runs existed to stop the scanner losing mail silently, but persistScanRun was called on the SUCCESS path only — in scan-imap, exactly once, at the end. Every failure return (missing auth, unauthorized, no connection, and both "IMAP connection failed" paths) returned before it. So the table recorded successes and nothing else. Let a photo scan admit it failed. photo_scan_jobs is written in exactly two places in lib/usePhotoLibraryScanner.ts: created as 'running' (~L479) and updated to 'completed' (~L1143), roughly 660 lines apart. Between them the media-library scan can throw (~L833: logs, sets local UI state, RETURNS) or the user can cancel (~L842: RETURNS) — neither touches the job row — and the app can simply be killed or backgrounded, which has no code path at all. So a job that dies stays 'running' for ever. In prod that is 36 rows across 12 of 14 users, averaging 5 days old, one user having never completed a single scan. And because scanned_assets is only written at completion, every running row reads 0 scan

Say WHY an import was rejected. That matters because 223 DISTINCT events were rejected and 151 of them exist nowhere in the owning user's collection. Some of those are marketing mail the AI correctly binned. The scanner is already correct about this — its already-handled set inner-joins tickets and excludes archived ones, so those assets become eligible again, and a single-ticket scan searches a window around the EVENT date rather than the incremental cursor, so age is not the problem either. Forward-to-Scan (Phase 0) — docs/forward-to-scan-plan.md A per-user inbound email address so people can FORWARD ticket confirmations instead of connecting their whole inbox (only ~9% ever connect one). A forwarded email is parsed and inserted by the SAME pipeline as a Gmail scan, tagged source='forward'.

Human-readable inbound addresses: <username>-<6 hex> instead of 12 random hex chars, e.g. rahul-a1b2c3@<inbound-domain> rather than e3ad78b86126@<inbound-domain>. SECURITY NOTE: this address is BOTH the routing key and the write credential for an account — a forwarded mail lands in whichever account owns the address it was sent TO, regardless of who sent it (the From header is spoofable and is deliberately not used for routing). The username half is public, so the random suffix carries the entire secret. Keep a suffix on it; never reduce this to a bare username.

Sender/domain picker (progressive consent for Gmail scanning). Which ticket-platform senders this user allows scan-gmail to read, chosen at the consent step (curated list in modules/tickets/utils/ticketSenders.ts). NULL (default) = no constraint: scan all trusted senders + subject matches, byte-identical to the pre-picker behavior, so every existing connection is unaffected. Stored on the connection row — not passed per request — so the scheduled (cron) scans honor the same choice as user-triggered ones.

SeatGeek + TickPick + Ticketmaster CSV import (ImportSongkickScreen order-history sources). A new source string always needs the CHECK constraint updated on BOTH tables (see 20260723120000_forward_to_scan.sql): pending_imports takes the row at import time, and tickets takes the same string verbatim at approval — miss either one and the flow fails at runtime with a constraint violation.

Two device-derived signals about each matched photo. On iOS the Photos app already maintains "Favorites" and "Selfies" smart albums; these flags carry that membership onto the proposal at scan time. is_favorite floats starred keepers to the top of the review list. is_selfie is a LABEL only — it never changes ranking (an event selfie is a keeper, not a throwaway); it just drives the scan's colour split and an optional "hide selfies" filter. Neither touches match_score. Default false, so every existing proposal (and every Android proposal, where these smart albums aren't exposed) ranks purely on match_score exactly as before.

1:1 direct messages between friends. Sends are RLS-gated to accepted friends and blocked across a user_block in either direction. Realtime-enabled so an open chat receives the other side's messages live.
Per-user privacy preferences backing the Privacy settings page. Enforcement is applied in the app's read paths (user search, friend profile, friend tagging).

Suggests friends who also have a ticket for the same event (matched by title) but are not yet tagged on the caller's ticket, so the owner can tag them and enable sharing. SECURITY DEFINER so it can see friends' tickets (RLS otherwise hides them), but it only ever returns rows for a ticket the CALLER owns and respects each friend's privacy: they must allow tagging, share their events, and not run an only_me archive. privacy_settings rows are sparse, so absent settings coalesce to the permissive defaults.
Child attendee rows represent private kid tags under the ticket owner's account. They must not inherit the friend-visible branch used by normal user attendee rows.

Time-capsule hand-over: preview + redeem. A parent-created child_claim_invites token lets the child (on a brand-new account of their own) inherit copies of the parent's tickets the child was tagged in. Age/consent policy is enforced at account creation (the normal Salty sign-up), not here.

Extend the time-capsule redeem so the child also inherits the PHOTOS on the tickets they were tagged in — not just the events. We loop per source ticket so each new ticket keeps its own photos; both photo rows point at the same object in the public `ticket-photos` bucket, so nothing is re-uploaded. Device-only photos (no storage_url) are skipped — they live on the parent's device and can't follow the child.

Preserve the user's original ticket title when auto-relabel renames an imported event to its canonical real-event name (see supabase/functions/relabel-event). Additive + nullable — existing rows and queries are unaffected; NULL means "never relabeled".
No policies: only the service role, which bypasses RLS, reads/writes this shared, non-user-specific cache; users never touch it.
Owner-entered stage start time per act (setlist row). Nullable, additive. Applied out-of-band via apply_migration per supabase/migrations/README.md (db push errors on drift).

Optional demographic fields on feedback (age group, gender, how they heard about Salty). Nullable, additive. Applied out-of-band via apply_migration per supabase/migrations/README.md. These sync to the "Beta Users Feedback" Airtable base via the feedback-to-airtable edge fn.

Perf advisor (unindexed_foreign_keys): add covering indexes for every foreign key that lacked one. Speeds up joins and FK/RLS lookups; all additive and reversible. Applied to prod via Supabase MCP apply_migration (version 20260803191544); this file keeps the local migration history in sync (no types/db.ts change — indexes only).

Perf advisor (auth_rls_initplan): wrap auth.uid() in (select auth.uid()) so it is evaluated once per query (as an initplan) instead of once per row. Semantics-preserving. Covers the policies added after the earlier initplan sweeps (direct_messages, privacy_settings, inbound_email_addresses). ALTER POLICY (not drop/recreate) so no policy is ever momentarily absent. Applied to prod via Supabase MCP apply_migration (version 20260803192206); this file keeps the local migration history in sync (no types/db.ts change — policy bodies only).

Perf advisor (multiple_permissive_policies): each (table, role, action) below had two PERMISSIVE policies, so both were evaluated per row. Permissive policies are OR'd, so merging each pair into a single policy with the conditions OR'd is exactly equivalent. Expressions are copied verbatim (including the (select auth.uid()) initplan form) and OR'd. One transaction, so RLS is never left with a coverage gap. Applied to prod via Supabase MCP apply_migration (version 20260803192941); this file keeps the local migration history in sync (no types/db.ts change — policy bodies only).

Perf advisor (multiple_permissive_policies): pending_imports had a FOR ALL policy ("Users manage own pending imports") duplicating the per-action pending_*_own policies (all "(select auth.uid()) = user_id"), so every action had two permissive policies. The four per-action policies cover the same access command-for-command (INSERT via WITH CHECK; SELECT/DELETE via USING; UPDATE via USING, whose value a null WITH CHECK inherits), so the FOR ALL is fully redundant. Drop it — no access change. Applied to prod via Supabase MCP apply_migration (version 20260803193724). Verified: expanding FOR ALL across its 4 actions, no (table, action, role) has >1 permissive policy anywhere in the public schema.

Perf advisor (duplicate_index): friendships had two identical UNIQUE constraints on (requester_id, addressee_id): friendships_unique_pair and unique_friendship. Neither is referenced by any foreign key (verified via pg_depend), so dropping one is safe — the other still enforces the pair's uniqueness. Keep friendships_unique_pair, drop the dup. Applied to prod via Supabase MCP apply_migration (version 20260803194121); this file keeps the local migration history in sync. No types/db.ts change (constraint/index only).

Aggregate version of suggest_event_attendees: across ALL of the caller's owned active tickets, list friends who also have the same event (matched by normalized title) but aren't tagged yet, so the app can proactively prompt "tag them". SECURITY DEFINER because RLS hides other users' tickets; privacy predicates mirror suggest_event_attendees exactly (allow_tagging + share_events + not only_me).

Add 'edm' as a selectable ticket/event category (beta feedback rec4Sq0: "Add Comedy and EDM to types" — Comedy already landed 2026-07-21, EDM was missing). category is constrained by a CHECK on BOTH tickets and events. They must stay in lockstep: creating/mirroring the event row for an EDM ticket would otherwise violate events_category_check. 'dining' is kept for the legacy alias already in the constraint; the client normalizes 'dining' -> 'restaurant'.

Pillar 3 (scan-pipeline permanent fix): make "no duplicate review row" a DB guarantee. dedup_key = canonical per-user event fingerprint (dedupeTitleKey|dayKey), computed by supabase/functions/_shared/eventFields.dedupKey at ingest. Ingestion paths insert with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, so a re-scan/re-sweep can't create a duplicate. NULL (title-less rows, and paths not yet adopting the key) is left unconstrained because NULLs are distinct.

Pillar 4.1: one observable ingestion surface. Unions the latest scan_runs row per (user, source) — gmail / imap / forward — with the latest photo_scan_jobs row per user (mapped to source='photo'), so "did the last scan work for this user, and where did the funnel drop off?" is answerable in one place. Admin/service-role diagnostics only.

Pillar 4.2a: head-of-line stall guard for the IMAP full sweep. A message that permanently fails to fetch holds the sweep cursor (correct: it prevents silent loss), but forever = a silent STALL that blocks all newer mail. This counter lets the scanner force-advance past a persistently stuck batch after a threshold (a recorded dead-letter), trading a few lost messages for an unblocked sweep. Reset to 0 on any progress, so the common path never sees it.

Refine scan_cron_health: separate the true "cron down" signal (NO run of any outcome recently — the scheduler itself stopped) from "no recent success" (runs happen but none succeed, usually just nobody-connected). Prod had 385 no_connection gmail rows, which showed the original single `stale` flag conflated the two. Drop+recreate because column order changes.

Pillar 4.4: population-level photo-scan health (the parallel to scan_cron_health for email). Per-user latest jobs already show in ingestion_health (4.1); this aggregates outcome distribution + the "stuck running" count across all jobs, so a reaper regression (rows left 'running' forever — the exact class photoScanJobPatch exists to end) is visible at a glance. The processed-asset set is already durable (derived server-side from photos + reviewed pending_imports), so no per-device ledger is needed to prevent reinstall re-floods. Admin/service-role diagnostics only (aggregates across all users; no user_id).

Pillar 4.4: server-side abandoned-photo-scan reaper. The existing reaper is client-triggered (runs only when a user starts a NEW scan), so a job abandoned by a user who never returns stays 'running' forever — prod already showed 28 such rows. This hourly sweep applies the SAME 6h threshold server-side, making photo-scan durability independent of the user coming back.

Rename gmail_connections.gemini_consent -> scan_consent (the AI-parsing consent is no longer Gemini-specific). RENAME COLUMN preserves the type/default/NOT NULL (boolean NOT NULL DEFAULT false). Applied to prod out-of-band as migration 20260808180624 by a concurrent change; this file records it so the repo's migration history matches prod and a from-scratch build lands it. NOTE: this migration and its client-code half (useTickets/TicketsScreen/types/db.ts, which read and write this column by name) MUST ship together — the DB was renamed ahead of the code once, which made the current build read a column that no longer existed.

Tag acceptance (docs/tag-accept-plan.md, phase 2): a status on each attendee row so a tagged user can accept/decline. Default 'accepted' grandfathers every existing tag (and any insert predating the pending flow) — nothing needs re-accepting. New tags will explicitly insert 'pending' (phase 3).

The 'talk' category (ticketed talks/lectures/conferences) was added to the app (lib/categories.ts) but never to this CHECK, so every write with category='talk' — manual add, event edit, review-import, photo-scan — was silently rejected by the DB. Add it. 'dining' stays for legacy rows even though the app no longer offers it.
Beta request: "Need to add College / Alma Mater". A free-text profile field on the user, surfaced through the existing public_profiles read path (non-sensitive, meant to be shared).

Remote "please update" gate. One row per platform; the team bumps latest_build when a new build ships (and min_build to force-update below a floor). The client compares its running build number and shows a prompt. Seeded inert (0/0) so it never prompts until configured.
Current release links + the known-latest ios build. GREATEST so re-applying never LOWERS a value the self-report below may have already raised.

Shared se

Proactively enrich recently-imported past tickets every 6 hours by calling the enrich-sweep edge function via pg_net. enrich-sweep finds past sports/theatre tickets (imported in the last 30 days) still missing their result/cast and runs the lookups — the same work the app does lazily on view, but ahead of time so data stays fresh. The Authorization bearer is the PUBLIC anon key (already shipped in the mobile client bundle); enrich-sweep does its privileged work with its own service-role env + the SERVICE_ROLE_JWT function secret. cron.schedule is idempotent (upsert by job name). Tag suggestions matched a friend's event to the caller's by TITLE ONLY (lower(trim(title))): a friend who saw the SAME show on a DIFFERENT date was wrongly suggested (beta: "friend tagging isn't taking date into account — Dave went to Hamilton on a different date"), and a "TICKET:"-prefixed title never matched its clean twin. Match instead on the canonical event identity — a shared catalog event_id, else normalized title + DAY — mirroring the client lib/eventTitle.eventDedupeKey. Also stop suggesting a friend we ALREADY share this event with in EITHER direction (they're tagged on ours, or we're tagged on theirs) — the "already on the ticket" report.

Shared event photo album (beta: "i don't see his photos"). Two co-attendees of the same event each keep their own ticket; the event view pools everyone's photos. A new privacy toggle (share_event_photos, OFF by default) governs whether YOUR event photos are visible to attendees. Friend-scope the pooled album: a co-attendee's photos are only pooled when they are an ACCEPTED FRIEND of the caller (and sharing). Otherwise two strangers who independently logged the same event would leak photos to each other. Matches "for friends, event-photo visibility is a privacy setting" — own photos always; a friend's same-event photos only if they turned sharing on.

A co-attendee's photo can only render on MY device if it has a storage_url (an uploaded asset); their local-only device_asset_id resolves to nothing here and would paint a broken cell. My OWN photos stay included even when local (MediaLibrary resolves them by device_asset_id).

Return the uploader (uploader_id) so the event gallery can group photos by who took them (beta: Chris — "it should separate the photos by person... what photos you took, what photos whoever took"). Friends who ALSO hold a ticket for the same UPCOMING event as the caller's ticket, so both can be notified "you're both going" (beta: Chris — notify when a friend is going to the same event, "without spamming every friend on every purchase"). Non-spammy by construction: it only ever matches on the same event identity, never broadcasts a purchase to all friends. SECURITY DEFINER to see friends' tickets (RLS hides them); returns rows only for a ticket the CALLER owns, only for an upcoming event, and respects each friend's privacy (share_events, not only_me). Matches on event identity (event_match_key: shared event_id, else title|day) like the tag-suggestion RPCs, not raw title.

Who actually played in the game (TheSportsDB's lineup endpoint, premium v2 with v1 fallback) — Chris's "click on the players". Normalized array of { name, position, team, home, substitute, photo, playerId }. Nullable: coverage is strong for soccer, sparse for US sports, so most rows stay null and the UI omits the "Who played" section.

The caller's own + accepted-tagged games whose stored lineup includes this player — powers "games you saw them in" on the player bio card (the cross-game payoff for tappable lineups). SECURITY DEFINER to read sports_stats/tickets past RLS, but gated to auth.uid()'s OWN games only, so it never leaks another user's attendance.

Per-player box score for a game (statsapi.mlb.com for baseball — keyless, official, has the per-player batting/pitching lines TheSportsDB lacks). Array of { playerId:'mlb:<id>', name, team, home, kind:'batter'|'pitcher', position, order, line, + structured stats for aggregation }.

Batting totals for a player across the caller's OWN + accepted-tagged games (from stored box scores) — "how many HRs did I see Jeter hit". SECURITY DEFINER to read past RLS, gated to the caller's games only. Batting-focused (the HR/hit ask); a pure pitcher returns games=0.

Sport-agnostic cross-game totals for a box-score player across the caller's OWN + accepted-tagged games: sums every numeric key in each entry's `stats` object (hr/h/rbi for MLB; pts/reb/ast for NBA; g/a/sog for NHL; passYds/rushTD… for NFL). Replaces the batting-only mlb_player_stats_with_you. SECURITY DEFINER, gated to the caller's games only.
Per-play highlight clips for a game (MLB content API / ESPN videos — both keyless). Array of { title, url, thumb }. Fetched alongside the box score, so box_score_checked_at also gates this.

Permanent, self-healing venue geocoding for tickets. ROOT CAUSE it fixes: geocode-venues was ONLY triggered opportunistically (a photo scan, or opening the map) and is RLS-scoped to one user, so a ticket created through any of the six creation paths (gmail / forward / calendar / photo-import / manual / event-details) whose owner never hit one of those flows kept null coordinates forever — in prod, 81 well-named venues across EVERY source had no coordinates. This adds a server-side sweep so every active ticket with a venue and no coordinates — existing AND future, from ANY source — gets geocoded automatically. pg_cron -> trigger_geocode_sweep() -> pg_net POST -> geocode-cron edge fn -> ticket

Permanent, self-healing sports RESULT resolution for tickets — the third enrichment sweep (theatre cast = enrich-cast-sweep, venue coords = geocode-sweep, sports results = this). ROOT CAUSE it fixes: a game's score is only fetched by sports-score-lookup, which ran OPPORTUNISTICALLY (client-side on event open), and enrich-sweep skips imports >30 days old (API-quota guard). Any past game whose event was never opened — especially older imports — never got a result. In prod, 38 past sports tickets had no result (the bulk of the admin's "pending"). pg_cron -> trigger_sports_result_sweep() -> pg_net POST -> sports-result-cron edge fn -> sports_tickets_needing_result() -> per-ticket sports-score-lo

UNIFIED ENRICHMENT PIPELINE — the permanent fix for the recurring "a derived field never got filled" class of bug (venue coords, sports results, cast, setlist, price, ...). ROOT CAUSE (hit three times): every derived field is fetched OPPORTUNISTICALLY, client-side, when someone opens the event. Anything never opened (or imported long ago) stays incomplete, and we kept bolting on a bespoke cron per enrichment (geocode-sweep, sports-result-sweep, enrich-cast- sweep) — whack-a-mole, and every manual backfill re-throttled an external API. THE FIX: one queue + one worker. Work is DISCOVERED server-side for every incomplete ticket (no trigger on the hot tickets-insert path — a periodic enqueue is

Fold cast + setlist into the enrichment pipeline (20260813230000). Adds two discovery predicates to enqueue_enrichment_jobs() and retires the standalone enrich-cast-sweep cron (its edge fns stay deployed but idle) — the enrichment-worker now handles cast (drives enrich-cast) and setlist (drives setlist-lookup) alongside geocode + sports_result. Nothing else changes; convergence and pacing are the pipeline's.

Add the `verify` enrichment kind: cross-verify a photo/physical-scanned ticket against its RETAINED source image and reconcile improve-only (fill missing / fix low-confidence, never overwrite a confident value). Only photo-sourced tickets with a stored ticket-photos image qualify; source_verified_at makes it run once per ticket.

No enrichment moves and no user-facing behavior changes here. Identity was validated read-only against live data before writing this:

============================================================================ Phase 1 — Sibling-copy enrichment dedup (setlist + cast) The FIRST ticket at a canonical event pays the external enrichment cost; every later sibling ticket at the SAME event copies that result instead of hitting setlist.fm / phish.net / Wikidata / Anthropic again. This is the read-through cache's core win, delivered without moving storage or touching the client: the enrichment worker calls these BEFORE its external fetch and skips it on a hit. Legacy rows — attached before setlist-lookup gained its artistNameMatches guard — put a real setlist on the WRONG artist: e.g. SOFI TUKKER's setlist 637082ef (its 12 songs) landed on Twenty One Pilots, Oasis, and Nine Inch Nails tickets, so one id spans four unrelated events. Rule: NULL every setlistfm_id that maps to MORE THAN ONE canonical event (event_canonical_key = title|day). Genuinely-shared ids on duplicate tickets of a SINGLE show (e.g.

============================================================================ Phase 2 (step 1) — extend sibling-copy dedup to sports_result + geocode Same win as the Phase 1 setlist/cast copy: the FIRST ticket at a canonical event pays the external cost, later siblings copy. No client changes — the enrichment worker calls these before its external fetch and skips it on a hit. ============================================================================

============================================================================ Phase 2 (step 2) — read-through RPCs for setlist + cast The client reads a ticket's setlist/cast THROUGH its canonical event, so a user-edited setlist (or a scanned playbill cast) converges to every attendee of the same show — not just the ticket it was entered on. RLS on setlists / ticket_cast is strictly own-ticket, so these SECURITY DEFINER RPCs do their own access check (caller must own or be tagged on the ticket) and pool only across own-or-attended tickets at the event (the connected-attendee boundary). Ranking picks ONE canonical source ticket: a user edit wins (convergence), then the caller's own row (so set

Later, enrichment reveals a reliable STRONG id — the TheSportsDB game id, or (now that its corruption is repaired) the setlist.fm setlist id. This canonicalizes those events: • re-key a fuzzy event to its strong key (g:<id> / sf:<id>), or • if a different event already owns that strong key, MERGE into it — collapsing e.g. "Giants Game" and "New York Giants vs Cowboys". Non-destructive: a merged loser is KEPT with merged_into set and its key

It's now stored on setlists.phishnet_show_id, and reconcile treats pn:<showid> as a trusted per-show strong key alongside g:<game> and sf:<setlist>. Applies to the Phish family only (small population), so mostly future-proofing. ============================================================================

Adds the streak_reminders channel, a once-per-user-per-month dedupe ledger, and the pg_cron job that drives the streak-nudge edge function. Mirrors the daily-digest cron wiring (20260709130000): pg_cron -> trigger_streak_nudge() -> pg_net POST with the shared scan_cron_secret.

One alert per (adder, recipient, event) — so a friend who keeps adding to the same event's shared album isn't re-pinged; they can open the album to see more. No new preference: this rides the existing friend_activity channel. No client reads this table (service-role writes only), but RLS is enabled + read-own for parity with the other sent_* ledgers.

Mirrors get_mutual_event_counts / get_friend_profile_stats: SECURITY DEFINER, returns only AGGREGATE COUNTS (never a friend's ticket rows), scoped to the caller + accepted friends. Counts avoid date_str parsing (free text) — total shows = distinct canonical events; venues = distinct venue name; shared_with_me = events both attended (0 for self).

Crew leaderboard: add a "this year" dimension + a normalized year on tickets. date_str is free text (no date column), and we only need the YEAR for "this year" ranking, so extract the 4-digit year rather than parse a full date. IMMUTABLE so it can back a STORED generated column that auto-maintains on insert/update and backfills existing rows.

Unify "shows together" across the Stats crew card and the Profile crew card. Previously they disagreed: the Stats card counted mutual tickets, the Profile card counted tags-by-me. One definition now: distinct events you were BOTH at by ANY signal — you both hold a ticket to the same canonical event, OR you tagged them on your ticket, OR they tagged you on theirs. SECURITY DEFINER + counts only (never a friend's rows), accepted-friends-gated.
Server-sync the taste-picker answers (were AsyncStorage-only) so they survive reinstall / follow the user across devices, and can feed Discover ranking. One row per user, own-row RLS.

"Your saved event is coming up" reminders. New channel + a once-per-event dedupe ledger + the daily cron. Date proximity is decided in the edge function (JS parse of free-text date_str), so no SQL date column is needed. Mirrors the streak-nudge cron wiring.

"Who else was here" people discovery — STRICTLY opt-in, off by default. A symmetric-consent pool: a user must set discoverable_at_events=true to APPEAR to others, AND must be discoverable to SEE others. So nothing about anyone's attendance is exposed until they explicitly opt in, and only to other opted-in co-attendees. Returns minimal public-profile fields only, never event history. PRIVACY: verified default=0, caller-only-opted-in=0 (a non-opted-in user is never revealed), both-opted-in+not-friends=1. Ship gated behind an explicit privacy review.

Price-drop alerts on saved events. Baseline price captured at save time (SavedEventsContext); the saved-event-reminders cron re-checks the current price (ticket-price-lookup) and notifies once on a meaningful drop. Best-effort — Ticketmaster omits prices on many events.

Stores the pre-show AI-predicted setlist per ticket (a plain string[] of song names), captured when the user views the "likely setlist" on an upcoming show. After the show it's compared to the real setlist for a "you called N of M" scorecard. Own-rows RLS; a prediction never touches the setlists table (setlist-lookup's preview mode is no-persist), so it can't corrupt the real setlist.

Trip discovery is now an opt-in feature (Privacy → Photo scanning). This column gates whether the on-device photo scan looks for multi-day TRIPS in the user's camera roll and creates trip cards. OFF by default for EVERYONE, including users who already have trip tickets — there is intentionally no grandfathering. The flag governs FUTURE photo trip-discovery only: it never hides, removes, or reclassifies existing trip tickets (those stay ordinary rows in `tickets` and render as before). Night-event (concert/show) discovery and email/calendar ticket detection are unaffected.

adminLibs.name: airtable.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Read-only Airtable client for the "Beta Users Feedback" base (base id appUUEmdTAOl9ZmXV) — in-app feedback, synced from Supabase via the feedback-to-airtable edge function. This is the single source for the admin Beta Feedback dashboard (the TestFlight base is deliberately not read here). Leave AIRTABLE_API_KEY unset to disable the page (it shows a setup notice instead of erroring — same pattern as the v2 database / PostHog).

adminLibs.name: alerts.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Incident lifecycle and cascading notification for the health checks. The rule that makes this usable rather than noisy: **alerts fire on state transitions, not on state.** A check that has been down for six hours produced one tier-1 email when it broke, one tier-2 email when it stayed broken past the escalation window, and one "recovered" email at the end — not one per cron tick. Tier 1 is the first responder (Rahul). Tier 2 is pulled in only when tier 1 hasn't cleared the incident within `escalate_after_minutes` — the "what if he's travelling" case from the 8/15 review.

adminLibs.name: anthropic.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Salty's edge functions call Anthropic over raw fetch with a forced tool call (see enrich-cast); the admin app has no SDK installed, so we mirror that proven pattern — no new dependency, and it's known to work on this account's key.

adminLibs.name: api-usage.ts
adminLibs.purpose: The external-API ledger (`api_usage_log`), written by the edge functions' trackedFetch wrapper. Sibling to lib/llm/log.ts, but for the OTHER side of the bill: Ticketmaster, TheSportsDB, setlist.fm, Spotify, Nominatim, ESPN, MLB — the providers the product depends on that nothing was watching. The provider's own dashboard can tell you a quota is nearly spent; only this can tell you which edge function spent it. Every figure is aggregated in Postgres (016_api_usage_summary.sql). Reducing rows in JS would be silently wrong: PostgREST caps responses at 1000 rows on this project regardless of .limit(), and this table is already past 12k. Same trap as count_pending_import_users.

adminLibs.name: auth.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Per-admin page allowlist. null = unrestricted (level rules only). See lib/pages.ts.

adminLibs.name: categories.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Canonical ticket taxonomy for the admin panel — kept in sync with the app's source of truth at salty-mobile/lib/categories.ts. When the mobile app adds or renames a category or source, update THIS one file and every admin dropdown, filter, validator, chart, and emoji stays correct. History: the admin previously hardcoded a stale list (`dining`, and missing `edm`/`comedy`/`talk`) in ~8 places, which silently downgraded approved imports to `other` and blocked editing those tickets.

adminLibs.name: config-status.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Read-only client for the mobile project's `config-status` edge function — reports which server-side secrets are set (names + presence booleans only; secret VALUES are never returned). Auth is a shared secret sent as the `x-config-secret` header, so the powerful Supabase Management personal access token stays OUT of the admin app. CONFIG_STATUS_SECRET — shared secret; must match the same-named Edge Function secret set in the mobile Supabase project. Leave CONFIG_STATUS_SECRET unset to disable the mobile-secrets section (a setup notice shows instead — same pattern as the other optional integrations).

adminLibs.name: email.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Resend transport for admin-sent emails (product-update / announcement broadcasts and one-off per-user messages). Requires two env vars: RESEND_API_KEY — API key from resend.com EMAIL_FROM — verified sender, e.g. "Salty <updates@saltydigital.ai>"

adminLibs.name: errors.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Mobile crash / unhandled-exception feed, from PostHog's `$exception` events. Closes the last blind spot in the health picture. lib/health.ts pings edge functions for reachability and reads ingestion telemetry, but nothing surfaced errors happening ON DEVICE — a crash loop in the app was invisible to the admin panel entirely. PostHog is already collecting these (44 in the 30 days before this shipped), so this needs no new integration or credential, just a read. Grouped by PostHog's own `$exception_issue_id`, so the grouping matches what you'd see in PostHog's Error Tracking UI rather than a second, divergent definition.

adminLibs.name: events.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Helpers for the canonical-event surface (the `public.events` table the app resolves every ticket to). Mirrors the app's identity model: an event's `event_key` is a strong id when it carries a `g:`/`sf:`/`pn:` prefix, otherwise a fuzzy `title|date`. Precedence: g: (sports) > sf: (setlist.fm) > pn: (phish.net) > fuzzy.

adminLibs.name: format.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Format a ticket price. Returns '—' when no price is recorded.

adminLibs.name: health.ts
adminLibs.purpose: The health checks, extracted from the /health page so the cron job (/api/cron/health) runs exactly what the page renders. Two implementations would drift, and a monitor that disagrees with the dashboard is worse than none. Everything here is read-only — no check mutates state or triggers real work.

adminLibs.name: invite.ts
adminLibs.purpose: One-time invite / password-set token for the admin panel. Only the SHA-256 hash is persisted (admin_users.invite_token_hash). The raw token is embedded in the invite URL emailed to the invitee, so a DB leak never yields a valid, usable token — a matching URL is still required. 32 random bytes → 43-char base64url string; brute-forcing the hash space is not feasible.

adminLibs.name: message-templates.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Pre-written email + push-notification templates for the admin Email and Notifications pages. Picking one pre-fills the composer so common messages don't have to be typed from scratch — edit the fields before sending. Text in [square brackets] is a placeholder: swap it for the real detail before you send. Nothing here is substituted automatically. To add a template, append to the relevant array — the pickers pick it up automatically. Email bodies use blank lines to separate paragraphs (the branded renderer turns each blank-line-delimited block into a paragraph).

adminLibs.name: ops-cycle.ts
adminLibs.purpose: One full monitoring cycle: check → reconcile → remediate → verify → notify. Shared by the cron route and the "Run now" button on /health so both do exactly the same thing. The ordering matters: remediation runs *before* notification, and a verification pass re-reconciles afterwards. A transient blip that auto-heals within the cycle therefore resolves silently — nobody is emailed about a problem that no longer exists by the time the email would have been sent.

adminLibs.name: pages.ts
adminLibs.purpose: The canonical list of admin pages. Extracted out of components/sidebar.tsx so ONE table drives three things that must never disagree: what the sidebar renders, what the per-admin page allowlist offers, and what the proxy enforces. When they were separate, a page could be hidden from the nav while still being reachable by typing the URL. `maxLevel` is the CAPABILITY bar (1 = Super Admin … 4 = Support) and is unchanged. The allowlist layers ON TOP of it — it can only ever narrow access, never widen it. See canAccessPage().

adminLibs.name: pending-imports.ts
adminLibs.purpose: How many distinct users are behind the unreviewed-import backlog. `pending_imports` counts EVENTS, not people: one user with a linked inbox routinely contributes dozens, so the raw total reads as a user count and badly overstates reach. Every surface that shows the total shows this next to it. Counted in Postgres, not JS. PostgREST caps a response at `db-max-rows` (1000 on this project), so `select user_id` + a Set silently undercounts the moment the backlog passes that — and the backlog is already four figures.

adminLibs.name: posthog.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Read-only PostHog query client for admin analytics (build adoption, etc.). PostHog's ingestion ("project") API keys are write-only, so querying needs a **Personal API key** scoped to `query:read` (+ `project:read`): POSTHOG_API_KEY — personal API key (starts with `phx_`) POSTHOG_PROJECT_ID — numeric project id (defaults to 489677, the Salty project) POSTHOG_HOST — API host (defaults to https://us.posthog.com) The panel only ever runs read-only HogQL SELECTs against this connection. Leave POSTHOG_API_KEY unset to disable the feature — pages show a "not connected" notice (same pattern as the v2 database / Beta Signups page) instead of erroring.

adminLibs.name: remediation.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Auto-remediation for health incidents. The safety property that makes this acceptable against production: **the model never writes an action, it only chooses one from the allow-list below.** Every entry is a bounded, reversible operation that a human would run from the admin panel anyway. An LLM that returns anything not in this list is ignored and the incident escalates to a person instead. Deterministic rules run first and cover the cases we already understand. The model tier (lib/llm/ladder.ts) is only consulted for incidents with no matching rule, and only when `ai_triage_enabled` is on — so the common path costs nothing and behaves identically every time.

adminLibs.name: sort.ts
adminLibs.purpose: Server-side, in-memory row sorting for fully-loaded (non-paginated) tables that pair with the URL-driven <SortLink> header. Reads `sort`/`dir` from the page's searchParams; when no known sort key is set, falls back to `fallback` (typically newest-first). Nulls always sort last; strings compare numerically-aware.
